Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Probably derived from letä, the consonant stem for lentää (“to fly”), as *len(nä)ttö.[1]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈletːo/, [ˈle̞t̪ːo̞]
  • Rhymes: -etːo
  • Syllabification(key): let‧to
  • Hyphenation(key): let‧to

Noun

[edit]

letto

  1. fen, a type of treeless swamp

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈlɛt.to/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛtto
  • Hyphenation: lèt‧to

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Latin lectus (“bed”). Compare French lit, Galician and Portuguese leito and Catalan llit.

Noun

[edit]

letto m (plural letti or (Old Italian) letta, diminutive lettìno or lettùccio or letticciòlo, augmentative (uncommon) lettóne, pejorative lettàccio)

  1. (furniture) bed
  2. (potamology, hydrology) riverbed
Derived terms
[edit]
  • copriletto
  • lettaccio
  • letti a castello (“bunk bed”)
  • letti gemelli (“twin beds”)
  • lettino
  • letto matrimoniale (“double bed”)
  • lettone
  • lettuccio

See also

[edit]
  • giaciglio

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Latin lēctus, perfect passive participle of legō.

Participle

[edit]

letto (feminine letta, masculine plural letti, feminine plural lette)

  1. past participle of leggere (“to read”)

Anagrams

[edit]
  • lotte, tolte
